tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

start_coordinate.description: (x, y): The starting coordinates for `left_click_drag`.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app ("run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen"), not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch. When the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and boots one that is off, so do not boot a simulator yourself. 'launch' installs and launches a built .app. Build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app ("run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen"), not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch. When the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and boots one that is off, so do not boot a simulator yourself. 'launch' installs and launches a built .app. Build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user. Call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and it boots one that is off and returns while that one is still starting up. Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches: the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition: 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'set_posture' moves the hinge of an iPhone Duo (a simulator with a small outer screen and a large inner one) to 'state': 'closed' lights the outer screen, 'open' (flat) the inner one, and 'half_open' opens it to 'angle' degrees, where iOS picks the lit screen; the result says which. Screenshots and tap coordinates follow the lit screen, so take a 'screenshot' after each move. 'posture' reports the state, the hinge angle and the lit screen. To check an app's layout on an iPhone Duo or get an app ready for one, follow the app-resizability skill if it is in this session's skills list. Only skills listed in this session count, so do not search the disk for it. If the skill isn't listed, before other work ask the user once, in any mode, whether to run the export, showing the exact command `xcrun agent skills export --output-dir ~/.claude/skills` just before the question in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!" (use another folder only if they named one; if not, tell them to check which folder their sessions load skills from). Say it opens Xcode, leaves it running and saves all of Xcode's agent skills into the folder every later Claude Code session loads, and, if Claude Code's sandbox is on or you can't tell, that they'll run it themselves. Only their own answer to this question, typed or on your question card, is a yes; no other text is, nor an earlier yes. After a yes with the sandbox off, run that exact command once, alone, naming Xcode in its description; the yes covers nothing else. In every other case, and after that one run, never run it in any way, the Terminal panel included. After a no, go on without the skill. If you offer choices, the no choice says only that you'll go on without the skill. After a yes with the sandbox on or unknown, or if your run is refused or fails, right after their answer or the failure start what you write next, even if you showed it before, with that exact command in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!"; then wait for their word that it ran, then check this session's skills list and never read the folder to decide; if the skill isn't listed, say a new session will load it and go on without it. Only when the user asked to check or fix the layout on a Duo, not to review or read code: note the state and angle with 'posture'; for closed, half_open and open, call 'set_posture' and take a 'screenshot'; if the open screen shows the app with black bars and the target sets UIRequiresFullScreen, tell the user the key is the likely cause and keep it unless they ask; if the user agrees to a fix, make only that fix, then rebuild, 'launch' the app and check again; last, put the hinge back. 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag: left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator this session already uses, else a booted one no other session is using, else the first booted one. If none is booted, 'attach' boots the only one the user already allowed, and 'launch' does so or asks for 'attach' first; if there is not exactly one, name one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

angle.description: For 'set_posture' with state 'half_open': the hinge angle in degrees, 1 to 179 (0 is shut, 180 flat); default 130.

I've fixed JUSPRIN-APP-B ("The app did not select filament 2"). Before the fix, a request that couldn't work was checked as valid, then failed partway through and left the printer half changed. Now it's refused before anything changes. The change is one file, `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp`, on branch `claude/printer-setup-slots`. It builds and passes clang-tidy, and it isn't committed yet.

**What went wrong:** The project had three filament slots on a Bambu P1S. The model asked to switch to a Creality Ender-3 V3 KE and set two filaments. The preview checked the request against the three slots the project had and said it was fine. But when Orca switches printers, it replaces the filament list with the one last used on the new printer. With the "Remember printer configuration" setting on (the default), a printer you've never used gets one slot. So the switch left one slot, setting filament 2 failed, and the printer and process stayed switched.

**The fix:** When a request changes the printer, the preview now works out the slot count the switch will produce, using the same rule as Orca's switching code. That rule is:
- one slot, plus one for each filament the app remembers using on that printer;
- at least one slot per nozzle, unless the printer feeds every filament through a single nozzle.

If the request has more filaments than that, the preview says so, for example "With Creality Ender-3 V3 KE 0.4 nozzle selected, this project has 1 filament slot." The message for the no-switch case is unchanged, except that it now says "1 filament slot" instead of "1 filament slots".

**What I tested** on the rebuilt app, using the same three-filament P1S project as the reproduction:
- **The original request** (KE plus two filaments): the preview now flags it and the apply refuses it. The printer stayed on the P1S, so nothing was changed.
- **KE with one filament:** applied normally.
- **Back to the P1S, which the app now remembers with three filaments:** the preview predicted three slots, and the switch produced three.
- **No printer change:** four filaments on the three-slot P1S was refused, and three applied.

**Still open:**
- I haven't posted a Sentry note on APP-B or resolved it yet. I'll do that once the fix is committed, as with APP-D.
- After APP-B, the remaining inbox items are JUSPRIN-APP-A, and OBICO-SERVER-B2P, which can be resolved around 2026-11-26 if it stays quiet.
- You haven't answered my earlier question from the APP-D fix, which cherry-picked upstream OrcaSlicer's change. That change includes a dialog Windows users see when OpenGL fails to start, and it has never been run on Windows. Do we keep it or take it out?

content.content:
The printer chat asks for a serial number, login or printer name in its form

A Flashforge Creator 5 Pro in LAN Only mode could not be connected from the
printer chat (TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin issue 42). Its test needs the
printer's serial number and access code; without them the app tries TCP port
8899, which the printer refuses. PrusaLink set up with a user name and
password, and Repetier, which needs the printer chosen on the server, had the
same gap: the chat could only send an address and one key, so the AI sent
people to the classic printer settings window.

printer_host_connect now takes `ask`, one to three of the form's boxes:
apiKey, accessCode, serialNumber, userName, password, printerOnServer. With
`ask` the app opens the form at once and tests only once the person presses
Connect. The app decides which boxes hide what is typed (API key, access code,
password). Every value goes into the printer's own settings
(printhost_apikey, flashforge_serial_number, printhost_user,
printhost_password, printhost_port) and never reaches the model, which reads
only the outcome and whether the test sent typed or saved values. An empty box
keeps what the printer has saved for the same address and type. A user name
or password switches the printer to user and password sign-in.

The connect-print-host skill tells the AI to use the form for Flashforge,
PrusaLink with a login and Repetier; UltiMaker is the only type still sent to
the classic window. Kenneth: "The new form is part of this change", so the
skill and the form land together.

Also:
- The tool's argument check accepted only hostType and address, so a call
  with `ask` would have been refused before it ran.

content.text:
Yes, I reproduced the same error and confirmed the fix stops it, so it's landed and pushed. The fix is commit 0a3cf744f8 on jusprin-dev, and origin matches. JUSPRIN-APP-B is resolved in the next release.

**The Sentry event and my reproduction are the same failure.** The report came from one user on Windows, running JusPrin 2.0.1, on 2026-11-23:
- **What the AI did:** it ran `printer_setup_preview`, which said the request was fine. Then it ran `printer_setup`, which switched the printer to a Creality Ender-3 V3 KE and the process to the KE one, set filament 1, and stopped with "The app did not select filament 2".
- **Before the fix:** I opened a three-filament project on a Bambu P1S and asked for the same switch to the KE with two filaments. I got the same two steps and the same error, with the same printer, process and filament 1 left changed.
- **After the fix:** the same request is refused by the preview, and `printer_setup` refuses it too. The printer stayed on the P1S, so nothing was half changed.

The other checks also passed:
- The KE with one filament applies.
- Switching back to the P1S, which the app then remembers with three filaments, is predicted as three slots and gets three.
- Without a printer switch, three filaments apply and four are refused.

**What I couldn't match exactly:** the user's printer preset was named "Creality Ender-3 V3 KE" and their filament was "Generic PLA @System". In my test install they were "Creality Ender-3 V3 KE 0.4 nozzle" and a Creality generic PLA. I also tested on macOS, not Windows. The slot counting involved works the same on every platform, so I expect the result to hold there, but I haven't run it on Windows.

**In Sentry and Gmail:**
- I posted a note on the issue explaining the cause and the fix.
- The issue is now resolved in the next release. Events from 2.0.1 stay quiet, and an event from any newer release reopens it, which would mean the fix didn't work.
- The alert email is in the trash.

You haven't answered my earlier question from the APP-D fix, which cherry-picked upstream OrcaSlicer's change. That change includes a dialog Windows users see when OpenGL fails to start, and it has never been run on Windows. Do we keep it or take it out?

Should I start on JUSPRIN-APP-A next? Yes, or not now?

# Project chat prompt tests

The project chat's assistant is a system prompt
(`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts`), the project
tools and the chat. `run_prompt_tests.py` asks the live model for its next
step at a known point of a project chat and checks that step against one
sentence of the prompt. After an edit it runs once, on the checkout, and
prints each case beside a baseline kept in the repository (`baseline.json`;
see "Judging a prompt or skill change"). The app does not run.

On Kenneth's local machine, the keys are in
`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env` (outside the repository, mode `600`). An
agent running this suite can load them for that command in a subshell:

```bash
( . "$HOME/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env"; tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py )
```

Do not print, copy into the repository, or include the key values in a command
or test log. The file exports `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`; the
runner reads them from its environment. No run happens without Kenneth
approving that batch (case count, runs, token estimate). A `403 Key limit
exceeded` means stop; do not switch keys.

The model, hosts and judge are the printer suite's (`tests/printer_prompt`,
"Which model"): DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter, pinned to Alibaba,
Novita, Baidu and AtlasCloud, with a pinned OpenAI judge. `--backend
claude-cli` runs the same cases on the developer's Claude subscription
instead, for iterating on a prompt without API cost (see "Running on the
Claude subscription").

## One step, with its reads answered

Each case starts at a point recorded from the app and judges the model's next
step: a reply, or its tool calls. One response may hold several calls. The
app asks for that (`parallel_tool_calls: true`) and runs every call in the
order the model wrote it, so every call is judged here:

- A change anywhere in the response (any call the registry does not mark
  read-only) is the step, whatever came before it; the first change if
  there are several. It ends the run, and nothing is answered, with one
  exception below.
- A response of reads only is checked read by read, in order, and the first
  read the case decides on is the outcome: `issue-fix` passes on a
  `settings_get` of its setting sent after a `workspace_inspect`.
- When the case decides on none of the reads (such as `workspace_inspect`
  before a reply), every one is answered with the result the app gave for
  that read at the same point, each under its own call id, and the model is
  asked again, at most three times (`MAX_READS`, counted in responses). As
  the app does, a read after one whose result did not succeed gets the
  app's "not run" result instead.
- If any read of the response has no recorded answer, none is answered and
  the run ends unobserved, so the history never holds a call without its
  result. A fourth response of reads ends it unobserved too.

Two kinds of change are ever answered, each only in a case that says so
(`later`), because what matters there is what the model does next: a
`setup_record` with a plan and no purpose (`print-this-no-purpose` and
`print-hook-no-purpose`), and a `slice_start` (`print-hook-no-purpose`). `later`
maps what the run has done so far to the point recorded right after it, by a

content.content:
# Test suite rules

Rules for writing tests under `tests/`. [CATCH2.md](CATCH2.md) is the Catch2 reference. Building and running the suites is covered on the wiki, at <https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_test.html>.

## The suites

- `libslic3r`: the core library. Geometry, meshes, file formats, config and presets, Clipper, algorithms, data structures.
- `fff_print`: the FFF slicing pipeline, from a `Model` plus config through `Print` and `PrintObject` to emitted G-code.
- `sla_print`: SLA support-tree and pad geometry, support-point generation, raycast.
- `libnest2d`: 2D nesting and packing.
- `slic3rutils`: the Python plugin system and its slicing-pipeline bindings.
- `filament_group`: filament-to-extruder grouping, checked against golden files.
- `cli`: end-to-end runs of the built `orca-slicer` binary, Linux only. These tests carry the `RequiresApp` label, which the CI unit-test job excludes because it receives only `build/tests`; run them with `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release -L RequiresApp`.

## Building and running

Tests are off by default, so the build has to be told to include them.

- Windows: `build_win.bat -ds --run-tests`, which builds the dependencies and the tests and runs them (`-l -x` for the clang-cl and Ninja build CI uses)
- macOS: `./build_release_macos.sh -s -a arm64 -T`, which builds and runs them
- Linux: `./build_linux.sh -t`, then `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release`

Rebuild a single suite with `cmake --build build --config Release --target <suite>_tests`. Visual Studio, Xcode and the Ninja Multi-Config generator that `build_linux.sh` uses are all multi-configuration, so `ctest` needs `-C` on every platform; without it, tests registered with plain `add_test()` lose their labels and report "Not Run".

## Where a test goes

- Pick the suite by the production code the test exercises, not by how the test is written.
- A property of a class that holds with no `Print` involved belongs in `libslic3r`. Behavior that depends on print settings, or produces or consumes G-code or slicing state, belongs in `fff_print`.
- One file per subsystem, named `test_<subsystem>.cpp`. It owns every test for that subsystem, whether the test reads in-memory state or generated output.
- When you add a file, list it in that suite's `CMakeLists.txt` in the same change.

content.content:
## What keeps it faithful to the app

- **The system prompt** comes from the page's own source, through
  `tests/printer_prompt/render_prompt.mjs` (`"kind": "project"`) and the page's
  esbuild. This needs node and the AgentUI npm install. `--prompt-rev REV`
  renders it as it was at a git revision, 6b4b8b6188 or later (the commit
  that moved the prompt from C++ to the page, unchanged).
- **`project_tools.json`** is the tool list the app sends in the project chat
  with nothing attached. `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` fails when it
  drifts from the registry. Regenerate it with
  `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PROJECT_TOOLS=1 agent_bridge_tests '[project]'`.
- **Everything else in the request** is the app's: `requests.json`, recorded
  by the shell harness from `script.json`:

  ```bash
  build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness \
      --project-prompt-requests tests/project_prompt/script.json tests/project_prompt/requests.json
  ```

  The harness runs the real app on its two-plate fixture (Bambu Lab X1 Carbon
  0.4, Bambu PLA Basic, 0.20mm Standard, plate 1 sliced) with the project
  chat's real OpenAI adapter, but the adapter's requests go nowhere: each is
  answered with the next model output the script gives. The tools run for
  real, and the app builds every request itself: the earlier turns as
  `AgentHost::make_agent_request` replays them (calls with their results,
  whole), the
  new message as `OpenAIResponsesAgent::initial_input` builds it (the
  person's words, then the app's `<print_issue>` and `<workspace>` blocks,
  each a part of its own), a canvas issue's message and context, a file-load
  report, the file-loaded skill and the plate's picture on the
  request that first carries a load report, the print-issues skill on the
  request that carries a chip's message or first shows a slice's new
  warnings, the slice-failed skill on the request that first shows a
  refused or failed slice, the setup skill on the request that first
  carries a recorded or changed purpose or a setup change under one, and
  the live results of this turn's calls with the
  workspace block `AgentHost::continue_after_tool` adds. Arguments that need
  ids take them from the real previous result (`{{result/sessionId}}`) or the
  project (`{{workspace/activePlateId}}`). For each request it keeps, the
  harness checks the tools equal `project_tools.json` and the instructions
  equal `projectInstructions.fixture.txt`, then leaves both out of the file;
  the runner puts the rendered prompt and `project_tools.json` back. The
  script's `answers` list names the reads recorded at every point.
  `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` also checks every recorded result and
  answer against its tool's output schema.
- **Answered reads** are added as the app continues a turn: the model's own
  output items, then a result for every call under its call id, in the order
  the calls were written. Each answer carries the action id and workspace
  block of the recorded call. The request so far is repeated whole, a
  skill's text and picture included: on the Responses API the app keeps a
  fired skill in the chat's record (`fe70eea593`). A point's `appended` (in
  `requests.json`) counts the last items of its request that it appended to
  the chat's request before it.
- **Skills** (`AgentUI/src/skills/*/SKILL.md`) reach the model only in the
  recorded requests: the app adds one to the request where its event first
  reaches the model, and every later request of the chat replays it
  unchanged. The recorder checks that a point the script marks
  `"skill": "<name>"` appends that skill (and the plate's picture for
  `file-loaded`) to the chat's request before it, that no other point
  appends a skill or a picture, so an import's point appends the
  file-loaded skill alone, and that the next request of the same turn (the
## Running it

The runner and `test_steps.py` need the app's argument check built:
`cmake --build <build dir> --config <config> --target tool_call_check`. The
runner takes the newest one under `build/` (or `JUSPRIN_TOOL_CALL_CHECK`) and
stops when it is older than `ToolRegistry.cpp`.

By default every case runs 3 times (`RUN_BUDGET` 81 shared by the cases run,
at most 20 for one case alone); `--runs N` sets it. `--verbose` prints every
run's conversation. Usage is logged for every response on stderr and totalled
at the end.

A run ends with every case it ran beside the baseline (below). It exits 1
when a case is marked worse, 2 when nothing was judged (there is no baseline,
or the run's model, host or judge differs from the baseline's), 0 otherwise;
`--must-pass N` makes the exit code 1 when a case passes fewer than N runs
instead, as before baselines.
`--results FILE` also saves the run's counts in the baseline's form, and
`--compare FILE` prints a saved run beside the baseline again without sending
anything.

```bash
tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --render-only --prompt-rev 6b4b8b6188 > bodies.jsonl
```

prints every request body it would send and their sizes, and sends nothing.

All runs of all the cases run share one pool of `--jobs` workers (5 by
default, 3 for the claude-cli backend below), and each run's line gives its
wall-clock time.

## Request bodies as posted (`--request-log`)

`--request-log DIR` (with `--live-agent`, `--manual-live-agent`,
`--plan-journey` or `--project-prompt-requests`; `DIR` must be new or empty) writes each request

I've reproduced and fixed the app's side of JUSPRIN-APP-A, but I haven't yet shown that the AI recovers when given the clearer refusal; that needs a live model run, which needs your approval. When the AI sends a `setup_record` purpose (the chat's title) longer than 60 characters, the app now tells it how long the purpose is and what the limit is. The fix is on branch `claude/setup-record-refusal` in the worktree `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/opengl-context-crash`, and it isn't committed.

**What happened:** A Portuguese-speaking user on Windows, running JusPrin 2.0.1, asked for a print with a good finish and supports that come off easily. The AI called `setup_record` with a purpose of 63 characters, and the limit is 60. The app refused the call, but its refusal only said "The tool arguments do not match the registered contract", without naming the field or the limit. The app lets the AI retry twice per turn and ends the turn on the third refusal, which is the error Sentry received.

The Sentry event has no record of the refusals themselves, but the evidence points to three refused calls in a row:
- The error says it was the fourth request to the AI service in that turn.
- The breadcrumbs show three tool calls that worked before it, which take at least one request.
- The turn can only end this way on the third refusal.

**What I reproduced:** I fed the app's agent loop the exact arguments from the Sentry event three times, with no live model involved:
- **First two calls:** both got the generic refusal.
- **Third call:** the turn ended with the same `UnexpectedServiceAnswer` error and message.
- **With the purpose cut to 60 characters:** the same call passed, so the length was the only problem.

**The fix** is in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`. When any top-level text argument is over its schema limit, the refusal now names it, for example "purpose is 63 characters, and it takes at most 60." Characters are counted as a person reads them, not as bytes, the same way the purpose check already counted. I added a regression test with the user's purpose. All 632 agent tests pass, and clang-tidy passes.

**Decision needed:** should I run a live check that the model actually shortens the purpose when the refusal names the limit? The app can't prove that by itself; only the model's behaviour can. The repo's prompt tests say no live run happens without your approval.
- **What the check would do:** use the app's real project-chat prompt and tools, plus a Portuguese conversation ending in the AI's 63-character `setup_record` call and the app's refusal. It would ask DeepSeek V4 Flash, the app's "Standard" model, for its next step 10 times with the old refusal and 10 times with the new one. A run passes when the next call's purpose is 60 characters or fewer.
- **Cost:** a rendered project-chat request is about 49 KB, so 20 requests come to roughly 280,000 input tokens on your OpenRouter key. I haven't looked up the dollar price.
- **What it leaves out:** "Expert" (Claude Sonnet 5.5), the app's default. The test keys file has only OpenRouter and OpenAI keys, and Sentry doesn't say which model this user had.
- **Without it:** the fix rests on my expectation that a model told the limit will shorten the text. That expectation is reasonable, but it isn't verified.

I recommend the run. Should I run it, or skip it?

content.content:
## Running on the Claude subscription (`--backend claude-cli`)

`--backend claude-cli` answers every step with the locally installed Claude
Code CLI in headless mode (`claude -p`), billed to the developer's Claude
subscription instead of a per-token API key. `--judge claude-cli` moves the
judge there as well. Neither needs a key; both need the CLI logged in once
with `claude auth login`. The runner refuses to start a run the CLI would bill
to an API key (`apiKeySource` other than the login).

```bash
tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli --case advice-infill --runs 1
```

The model defaults to `claude-opus-5-5` at effort `medium`, both pinned so a
count moves only when the prompt does (`--claude-model`, `--claude-effort`,
`--claude-judge-model`). `--claude-keep DIR` keeps each run's session file,
tool list, MCP config and the CLI's event stream for reading afterwards.

### Which backend for what

- **Iterating on a prompt or skill: the subscription.** A strong model
  answering the app's real requests, with real tool calls, shows what the
  prompt itself causes: an ambiguous sentence, a rule two sections disagree
  on, a skill that invites the wrong call. It costs no API money, so it can
  be run as often as the subscription's usage limits allow. Those limits are
  shared with the developer's own Claude Code work; start with one case and
  keep `--jobs` small.
- **Before a release: a small paid run on the app's default model.** The app
  defaults to `gpt-5.4-mini` (the OpenAI provider's default in
  `ProviderProfile.hpp`), which scored about like DeepSeek V4 Flash in the
  printer suite's model table (82 and 79 of 87, `tests/printer_prompt`,
  "Which model"). A strong model
  can paper over an ambiguity a weaker one trips on, so a pass on Opus does
  not show the shipped default will pass. That run needs Kenneth's approval
  like every paid batch.
- **The baselines** are DeepSeek V4 Flash with the OpenAI judge
  (`baseline.json`), except the subscription baseline, which is claude-cli's
  own (`baseline-claude-cli.json`, which `--backend claude-cli` compares with).
  A claude-cli count is compared only with that one. Changing the judge
  changes what every judged case counts, so the runner will not compare a
  run on another judge with either: such results start their own baseline,
  under the same "confirmed results become the baseline" rule.

### How a recorded request reaches the CLI

`claude_cli.py` turns each recorded request into a CLI run, and
`claude_mcp_stub.py` serves the tools:

- **System prompt**: the rendered prompt, as `--system-prompt`.
- **Tools**: the stub is a stdio MCP server with the case's tools (the 29 of
  `project_tools.json`, or the point's own list), with their real
  descriptions and schemas. Every call the model makes reaches the runner
  through it, and the step rules above apply unchanged: a read is answered
  with the recorded answer, a change ends the run (the runner stops the CLI;
  nothing is answered), a response of reads decides or is answered whole.
- **Web search**: the CLI's own `WebSearch` is offered before the stub's
  tools, as the app offers its provider's own search after its tools on every
  reply request (since 2026-11-03). The CLI runs a search itself inside the
  response, so the runner sees only its query and the pages it found; a
  response whose only calls are searches is read on to the reply that follows.
- **History**: the request's items before its last turn are written as a
  session file the CLI resumes (`--resume <file>`), so earlier messages,
  calls and results reach the model as its own turns, tool calls and tool
  results, not as a transcript. The last turn's message (the person's words,
  the `<workspace>` block, the plate's picture) goes in as one stream-json
  user message.
- **A point recorded mid-turn**, after a tool result (`after-preview`,
  `after-apply`, `after-slice`, `after-intent`, `direct-change-applied`,
  `direct-change-failed`, `first-person`, `slice-refused-by-tool`): the
  session ends on that turn's last call, marked as a deferred call. The CLI
  runs it through the stub, which returns the recorded result, and then asks
  the model.

Nothing from the developer's own Claude Code setup reaches the model: no
CLAUDE.md, auto-memory, settings, hooks, output style, skills, other MCP
servers or built-in tools other than `WebSearch`, a minimal environment, and an empty temporary
working directory. `test_claude_cli.py` checks that, and the shapes above,
by running the installed CLI against a fake Messages endpoint on localhost
(no login, nothing sent; about 10 seconds). Run it after a CLI update: the
session file is the CLI's internal format, verified against 2.1.283.

What differs from the app's request, beyond the model:

- **Developer messages.** The Messages API has no developer role, so each of

"""The claude-cli backend of run_prompt_tests.py: one recorded step answered by
the locally installed Claude Code CLI in headless mode, on the developer's
Claude subscription instead of a paid API key.
How a recorded request reaches the model:
  - instructions: the CLI's --system-prompt. The CLI puts two lines of its own
    before it (a billing header and "You are a Claude agent, built on
    Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK.") and adds a short "# Environment" block
    after the first message (working directory, platform, date, model name).
  - tools: the stub MCP server (claude_mcp_stub.py) serves the case's tools
    with their real descriptions and schemas. The model sees each under the
    CLI's MCP name, mcp__jusprin__<name>; the runner strips the prefix.
  - input: everything before the request's last turn is written as a
    session file the CLI resumes (--resume <file>), so earlier messages,
    calls and results reach the model as real turns, tool calls and tool
    results. The last turn's message (the person's words, the <workspace>
    block, the plate's picture) goes in on stdin as one stream-json user
    message. A developer-role item becomes a user text block wrapped in
    <developer_message> tags: the Messages API has no developer role.
  - a point recorded mid-turn (the request ends on a tool result) resumes a
    session whose last call is marked deferred: the CLI runs that call
    through the stub, which returns the recorded result (and the app's
    developer notes after it, as further text blocks of the same result),
    and then asks the model, adding its own "Continue from where you left
    off." after the result.
Every later call goes through the stub to the runner, which answers it with
answer() or ends the run by closing the process.
  - web search: the app offers its provider's own search on every reply
    request, so a run offers the CLI's WebSearch, the one built-in tool it
    has. The CLI runs a search itself; its query, the pages it found and the
    result the model read come back as a web_search output item, and the
    model goes on. A search in the history is resumed as the CLI's own call
    and result, as the app sends a response's items back.
Nothing from the developer's own Claude Code setup reaches the model:
--setting-sources "" (no settings, hooks or output style), no CLAUDE.md and no
auto-memory (environment), --disable-slash-commands (no skills),
--strict-mcp-config (only the stub), --tools "WebSearch" ("" for the judge:
no other built-in tool), a minimal environment, and an empty working
directory."""
import json
import os
import pathlib
import queue
import shutil
import signal
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time
import uuid
HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
STUB = HERE / "claude_mcp_stub.py"
SERVER = "jusprin"
PREFIX = f"mcp__{SERVER}__"
# The tool the CLI adds for --json-schema.
STRUCTURED_OUTPUT = "StructuredOutput"
# The CLI's own search, which a run offers as the app offers its provider's.
WEB_SEARCH = "WebSearch"
# For an offline check against a fake Messages endpoint: its URL. The CLI is
def split(items):
    """(history, last message, deferred call) for a recorded request.
    A request that ends on the person's message (with the app's notes after
    it): the history is everything before that message. One that ends
    mid-turn on a tool result: the history runs to the last call, which is
    deferred, and its result and the notes after it are the deferred answer."""
    end = len(items)
    while end and items[end - 1].get("role") == "developer":
        end -= 1
    if end and items[end - 1].get("type") == "function_call_output":
        output, call = items[end - 1], items[end - 2]
        if call.get("type") != "function_call" or call["call_id"] != output["call_id"] or \
                items[end - 3].get("type") == "function_call":
            raise ValueError("a mid-turn point must end on one call and its result")
        notes = [block["text"] for item in items[end:] for block in user_blocks(item)]
        return items[:end - 1], None, (call, [output["output"]] + notes)
    start = end
    while start and items[start - 1].get("role") in ("user", "developer"):
        start -= 1
    return items[:start], items[start:], None


def session_file(path, history, cwd, deferred):
    """A session the CLI can resume: the history as a chain of entries, and
    the deferred call's marker when the point is mid-turn."""
    session, parent, lines = str(uuid.uuid4()), None, []

    def add(kind, **fields):
        nonlocal parent
        entry = {"parentUuid": parent, "isSidechain": False, "userType": "external", "cwd": str(cwd),
                 "sessionId": session, "version": "2.1.283", "type": kind, "uuid": str(uuid.uuid4()),
                 "timestamp": "2026-10-19T00:00:00.000Z", **fields}
        lines.append(json.dumps(entry, ensure_ascii=False))
        parent = entry["uuid"]

    for index, message in enumerate(messages(history)):
        if message["role"] == "assistant":
            add("assistant", message={"id": f"msg_recorded_{index}", "type": "message", "role": "assistant",
                                      "model": "recorded", "content": message["content"],
                                      "stop_reason": "tool_use" if message["content"][-1]["type"] == "tool_use"
                                      else "end_turn", "usage": {"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0}})
        else:
            add("user", message=message)
    if deferred:
        call = deferred[0]
        add("attachment", attachment={"type": "hook_deferred_tool", "toolUseID": call["call_id"],
                                      "toolName": PREFIX + call["name"],
                                      "toolInput": json.loads(call.get("arguments") or "{}"),
                                      "hookName": "settings", "hookEvent": "PreToolUse", "permissionMode": "default"})
    path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


def key(name, arguments):
    return name + " " + json.dumps(arguments, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))


# --- One run ------------------------------------------------------------------


class Run:
    """The CLI answering one recorded request, response by response.
    next_response() returns the model's next response as Responses API
    output items; answer() gives the results of its calls, and the CLI asks
    the model again. close() ends it, whatever it is doing."""

    def __init__(self, instructions, tools, items, model, effort, keep=None):
        self.directory = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="jp-cli-", dir="/tmp"))  # a short socket path
        self.keep = keep
        self.events = queue.Queue()
        self.answers, self.answers_lock, self.closed = {}, threading.Condition(), False
        self.usage = []
        self.started = time.monotonic()
        cwd = self.directory / "cwd"
        cwd.mkdir()
        (self.directory / "tools.json").write_text(json.dumps(tools), encoding="utf-8")
        self.socket_path = str(self.directory / "s")
        (self.directory / "mcp.json").write_text(json.dumps({"mcpServers": {SERVER: {
            "command": sys.executable, "args": [str(STUB), str(self.directory / "tools.json"), self.socket_path]}}}))
        history, last, deferred = split(items)

    return len(text)


def one(wording, index):

    if first["name"] != "setup_record":
        return wording, index, "other call", first["name"] + " " + first.get("arguments", "")[:200]

    if "purpose" not in sent:
        return wording, index, "setup_record without purpose", json.dumps(sent, ensure_ascii=False)[:200]
    purpose = sent["purpose"]
    verdict = "fits" if characters(purpose) <= 60 else "too long again"
    return wording, index, verdict, f"{characters(purpose)} chars: {purpose}"


with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(jobs) as pool:
    futures = [pool.submit(one, wording, index) for wording in WORDINGS for index in range(runs)]
    results = [future.result() for future in futures]
for wording, index, verdict, detail in sorted(results):
    print(f"{wording} run {index + 1}: {verdict} | {detail}")

**What I ran:** the app's real project-chat system prompt and tools, with the project's real recorded workspace and object analysis. Then the AI's `setup_record` call with a 63-character Portuguese purpose, the app's refusal, and a request for the model's next step. The new refusal text is the one the built app produces.

**Results** (a run counts as fixed when the next `setup_record` purpose is 60 characters or fewer):

| Model | Old refusal (names nothing) | New refusal (names the length and limit) |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Opus 5.5 | 5 of 5 fixed | 5 of 5 fixed |
| Claude Sonnet 5.5 (production's "Expert") | 4 of 4 fixed, 1 ended on a read I had no answer for | 5 of 5 fixed |

Both Claude models fix the purpose even when the refusal names nothing. My guess is they read the `maxLength: 60` in the tool's schema, but that's inference.

**What this means:** I've reproduced the app's part of the failure. The app gives a refusal that names nothing, and the turn ends on the third refusal. I have not reproduced the part where the AI resends the same over-long purpose, so this run doesn't show that the fix matters. My hypothesis is that the user was on "Standard", which is DeepSeek V4 Flash, a weaker model than the Claude ones. I haven't checked which model they used.

**How the conversation differs from the user's:** the repo's test project is a 20 mm cube. With the user's own request (a decorative ear), the model kept noticing the mismatch and stopped to ask the person. So the request and the purpose describe the cube, still in Portuguese and still exactly 63 characters. The AI's refused call also carries only the purpose, without the user's plan, for the same reason.

content.content:
On Windows, a shown canvas whose context cannot be made current is reported once: wx drops the
wglMakeCurrent error in release builds, so the call is repeated to log GetLastError() with the
canvas's pixel format and the display it is on. If OpenGL never came up in the session, the
user gets one error dialog instead of an empty 3D view with no explanation. A GTK canvas can
fail until its surface is mapped, so other platforms only get the crash fixes.

* Name the Display Adapter Instead of Only Suggesting a Driver Upgrade When OpenGL Can't Be Activated

A context that can't be made current has several causes: no OpenGL driver
behind the display the window is on (a disabled adapter, or one running on
the Microsoft Basic Display Adapter), a broken driver, or an overlay. The old
advice to upgrade the driver covered only one of them. The dialog now names
the adapter Windows reports for the window's display and lists the general
checks, and the log line keeps the display device and adapter name.

(cherry picked from commit 3c72223aaf7976bdece51d125e5364d219c3d91f)


diff --git a/src/slic3r/GUI/GLCanvas3D.cpp b/src/slic3r/GUI/GLCanvas3D.cpp
index 8094704f56..625b102921 100644
--- a/src/slic3r/GUI/GLCanvas3D.cpp
+++ b/src/slic3r/GUI/GLCanvas3D.cpp
@@ -2557,7 +2557,13 @@ void GLCanvas3D::_render_frame(bool scene_dirty, bool only_init)
         return;
 
     // ensures this canvas is current and initialized
92:+// call to read the error, and add what the driver was given: the pixel format and the display adapter.
135:+    // The cause varies (no OpenGL driver behind the display, a disabled or broken driver, an overlay),
138:+    wxString message = _L("OpenGL could not be activated for the 3D view, so it cannot be shown.");
142:+        message += format_wxstr(_L("The window is on a display driven by \"%1%\"."), display.adapter);
145:+    message += _L("Make sure the display adapter driving this window's display is enabled and its driver is installed and up to date.");
147:+    message += _L("If the computer has more than one graphics card, connecting the monitor to another one may help.");
149:+    message += _L("If the problem remains, close any overlay or screen capture software and try again.");
150:+    // show_error() defers the dialog, so it does not open inside the paint handler drawing the canvas.
151:+    show_error(nullptr, message);

content.text:
The worktree is gone. Git removed it, and I deleted the Finder files left behind. Its branch is deleted too, and both fixes are on jusprin-dev.

**The Windows dialog.** The APP-D crash fix was a straight cherry-pick of upstream OrcaSlicer's commit, which fixes two crashes and also adds a Windows-only error message. Suppose someone on Windows opens JusPrin on a machine where OpenGL can't start for the 3D view, say a disabled graphics adapter or the Microsoft Basic Display Adapter. Before, they saw an empty 3D view with no explanation. Now they get one dialog per session: "OpenGL could not be activated for the 3D view, so it cannot be shown." It goes on to name the display adapter Windows reports, suggests enabling or updating that adapter's driver, suggests trying another graphics card if the computer has one, and suggests closing overlay or screen-capture software.

**Decision needed:** should JusPrin keep this dialog? It's live on jusprin-dev now and will ship in the next release unless removed. It's your call because JusPrin's rules say an error message that people can act on needs your yes.
- **Keep it:** the cost is that nobody has seen it on Windows, and its four sentences aren't in JusPrin's translation catalogs, so everyone would see it in English until they're added.
- **Remove it:** this means a JusPrin-only change in an OrcaSlicer-owned file, which the fork rules ask to keep minimal. People would be back to a blank 3D view with no explanation.

My pick is to keep it and add the translations. Should I do that, or remove it?

**OBICO-SERVER-B2P** was not a real user error. On 2026-11-23, an agent on this machine sent a `curl` POST with an empty body to the new `/ent/jusprin/v2/launches` endpoint, from your IP. That endpoint only expects the desktop app, and it runs `json.loads` on the body, so the empty body raised `JSONDecodeError`. I had planned to resolve it after three quiet days. On 2026-11-15 you told me to delete issues like this instead, so I deleted it (Sentry now returns 404 for it) and trashed its alert email.

That leaves a conflict. The triage skill's rule for your own requests (`references/auto-ignore-rules.md`) still says to resolve them after three quiet days, while you told me to delete one-off issues. Should I change that rule so a test request made from this machine is deleted the same day? Yes, or leave the rule as it is?

# JusPrin's translations JusPrin shows its interface in the languages OrcaSlicer ships a catalog for (`languages.json`). OrcaSlicer's own windows translate through upstream's catalogs in `localization/i18n/`, which the fork never edits. JusPrin's own text has catalogs of its own here, so taking a new OrcaSlicer release never conflicts in a translation file: | Text | Marked with | Catalog | How it reaches the app | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Native windows and text the native side sends to a page | `_L`, `_u8L`, `L`, `_L_CONTEXT`, `_L_PLURAL`, `translated_plural` | `native/.po`, template `native/JusPrin.pot` | `Brand/brand_catalogs.py` merges it into `resources/i18n//.mo`, the catalog the app loads | | The AI and Home pages | Lingui macros: `t`, `plural` from `@lingui/core/macro`; `Trans`, `Plural` from `@lingui/react/macro` | `pages/.po`, one for both pages | `@lingui/vite-plugin` compiles every catalog into each page; the page reads `?lang=` (`AgentUI/src/i18n.tsx`) | Native text that OrcaSlicer's template already has is left out of `native/JusPrin.pot`; upstream's translation is used. ## Updating the catalogs After marking or changing text: ```bash python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py ``` It runs `xgettext` over the native sources and Lingui's extractor over the pages, then merges the new entries into every language. Translate each new entry in every `.po`, following the editing rules in the repository's `AGENTS.md` (Localization & translations): keep every placeholder and line break, give each plural form its own inflection, and mark machine translations `# AI Translated`, adding `# Needs human review: ` where the meaning or the wording is uncertain. `AgentUI/src/catalogs.test.ts` fails while any entry is untranslated or a translation loses a placeholder. The page catalogs use ICU placeholders: `{0}`, `{name}`, numbered tags like `<0>…` for elements inside a `Trans`, and `{count, plural, one {# printer} other {# printers}}` for counts. Keep the placeholder and tag names; translate the words, including the words inside a plural's branches, and give the plural the categories the language uses (`one`, `few`, `many`, `other`). ## Marking text Mark every string a person reads: labels, buttons, headings, menu items, tooltips, `aria-label`s, placeholders, empty states, confirmation and error text. Do not change the English: marking must leave the source text exactly as it was. Leave these in English, unmarked: - **Text the AI model reads**: prompts, skills, tool descriptions and tool results, the project and printer instructions, anything that goes into a request to a model. The model speaks the person's language on its own, and `wording.test.ts` guards that text. When the same string is shown to the person and also sent to the model, translate it only where it is shown. - Identifiers and values the code compares, protocol fields, CSS classes, test ids, file names, URLs, setting keys, G-code. - Log lines and the text of error reports (`report_unexpected`, `report_error`): they are read by developers. - Names: JusPrin, OrcaSlicer, Bambu Lab, printer and filament model names. ### In the pages ```tsx import { t, plural } from '@lingui/core/macro'; import { Trans } from '@lingui/react/macro';

Takes effect when {app} restarts. Your project is saved first.

const label = plural(count, { one: '# printer', other: '# printers' }); const title = t({ message: 'Back', context: 'navigation' }); // a word with several meanings const hint = t({ message: 'Fit', comment: 'Verb: scale the model to the plate' }); // a note for translators ``` - One message per sentence. Never build a sentence from translated pieces, and never splice a translated word into another sentence: use a placeholder, or a `Trans` with the element inside it. - A count needs `plural` / `Plural`, not "printer(s)". - Put only plain variables in placeholders (`{name}`, not `{a.b.c}`): the translator sees the variable's name. Pull an expression into a well-named local first. - The language is chosen before the first render and never changes while a page runs, so `t` works anywhere, including at a module's top level and in plain `.ts` files. `Trans` and `useLingui` from the macros need no provider (see `i18n.tsx`). - Tests run in English, so a test that finds text by its English words keeps working. ### In the native code - `_L("…")` gives a `wxString` for a window; `_u8L("…")` gives UTF-8 for JSON sent to a page. - Translate when the text is used, never in a static initializer, which runs before the language is loaded. Mark such a table with `L("…")` and call `_L`/`_u8L` on the entry where it is shown. - Use `format(_L("%1% is too close to others"), name)` rather than concatenation, and `_L_PLURAL` for counts; `// TRN` above a string tells the translator what it means. - Every file that marks text is extracted: `update_catalogs.py` reads every `.cpp` and `.hpp` under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin` except `Testing/`. Do not add JusPrin files to `localization/i18n/list.txt`.

def keep_if_only_date_changed(path, before):
    """Leave a file as it was when only its creation date moved."""
    if before is not None and path.exists() and DATE.sub("", path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) == DATE.sub("", before):
        path.write_text(before, encoding="utf-8")


def native_sources():
    files = []
    for f in sorted(JUSPRIN.rglob("*")):
        if f.suffix in (".cpp", ".hpp") and not SKIP_DIRS.intersection(f.relative_to(JUSPRIN).parts):
            files.append(str(f.relative_to(ROOT)))
    return files


def upstream_header_line(lang, name):
    po = UPSTREAM_I18N / lang / f"OrcaSlicer_{lang}.po"
    m = re.search(rf'^"{name}: (.*)\\n"$', po.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), re.M)
    return m.group(1) if m else None


def update_native():
    NATIVE.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    pot = NATIVE / "JusPrin.pot"
    before = pot.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if pot.exists() else None
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        tmp = Path(tmp)
        listing = tmp / "files.txt"
        listing.write_text("\n".join(native_sources()) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        everything = tmp / "all.pot"
        run("xgettext", *XGETTEXT_KEYWORDS, "--add-comments=TRN", "--from-code=UTF-8", "--no-location",
            "--boost", "--no-wrap", "--package-name=JusPrin", "-f", str(listing), "-o", str(everything), cwd=ROOT)
        # Entries OrcaSlicer's template also has keep upstream's translations.
        shared = tmp / "shared.pot"
        run("msgcomm", "--more-than=1", "--no-wrap", "-o", str(shared), str(everything),
            str(UPSTREAM_I18N / "OrcaSlicer.pot"))
        if shared.exists():
            run("msgcat", "--unique", "--no-wrap", "-o", str(pot), str(everything), str(shared))
        else:
            shutil.copy(everything, pot)
    text = pot.read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace("charset=CHARSET", "charset=UTF-8")
    pot.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    keep_if_only_date_changed(pot, before)

    for lang in languages():
        po = NATIVE / f"{lang}.po"
        before = po.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if po.exists() else None
        if not po.exists():
            # A new language starts as the template's header alone, with
            # upstream's plural rule; msgmerge then adds every entry with as
            # many plural forms as that rule has.
            header = pot.read_text(encoding="utf-8").split("\n\n", 1)[0] + "\n"
            plural = upstream_header_line(lang, "Plural-Forms") or "nplurals=2; plural=(n != 1);"
            header = header.replace('"Language: \\n"', f'"Language: {lang}\\n"')
            header = re.sub(r'"Plural-Forms: .*\\n"', lambda _: f'"Plural-Forms: {plural}\\n"', header)
            header = header.replace("#, fuzzy\nmsgid \"\"", "msgid \"\"", 1)
            po.write_text(header, encoding="utf-8")
        run("msgmerge", "--quiet", "-N", "--no-wrap", "--previous", "-U", "--backup=none", str(po), str(pot))
        keep_if_only_date_changed(po, before)

import json, urllib.request
TOKEN = "REDACTED"
notes = {
 1611: """**By Claude Code** — **Merge (2026-11-24):** OBICO-SERVER-B2S (2118) merged in; the Merged Issues tab shows these two fingerprints only.
**Why now:** a JusPrin 1 user (JusPrin/v01.10.01.50, Windows, user 263168) hit it on release 4136. Our code: no change to the JusPrin 1 chat chain found; this is the same failure as July to September.
**Cause (hypothesis):** `determine_slicing_settings_step` asks the model to return `print_process_preset_name` from a list, and the validator compares strings exactly. Both names carry a 3MF file name decoded with the wrong encoding, with C1 control characters in it (`\\x98`, `\\xa0` here; `\\x8f`, `\\x9d` before). The model's copy of the name likely loses those invisible characters, so it never matches and instructor gives up after its retries.
**Impact:** 10 events, 2 users since 2026-07-10; the chat message fails.
**Classification:** needs attention, JusPrin 1 only. Possible fix (proposal): match the returned name after normalising or stripping control characters, or have the model return an index into the list.""",
 2115: """**By Claude Code** — **Triage (2026-11-24):** Android app 2.42 (Galaxy S24+, Android 17) crashed in `PrinterItem` (`src/screens/PrinterList/PrinterItem.js:48`): `primaryWebcam.name` is read while `primaryWebcam` is undefined. That happens when a printer has webcams but none is `is_primary_camera`, or has no webcams list at all (the `_.find` returns undefined).
**Why now:** Our code: 2.42 (build 336) shipped 2026-11-11 and is the first build with working source maps, so this may be an old crash under a new fingerprint. Dependencies: none. Client/environment: one Android user. Really new: probably not; see OBICO-MOBILE-21A.
**Related:** OBICO-MOBILE-21A has the same message inside the same React-Redux selector run (`checkForUpdates`) on iOS 2.33/2.40 and Android 2.40/2.41, 22 events and 12 users since April, but its stack has no app source lines, so I did not merge them.
**Impact:** 1 event, 1 user; the printer list crashes.
**Classification:** needs attention. Fix (proposal): `primaryWebcam?.name` in that selector.""",
 777: """**By Claude Code** — **Cross-reference (2026-11-24):** OBICO-MOBILE-24S is the same message on Android 2.42 with source maps, and points at `src/screens/PrinterList/PrinterItem.js:48` (`primaryWebcam.name` with no primary webcam). This issue's stacks are unsymbolicated, so it is likely, not confirmed, the same line; not merged.""",
 2120: """**By Claude Code** — **Triage (2026-11-24):** Whispr Notes iOS 0.7.11 (71) hung for at least 2 s at launch inside the Singular attribution SDK: `+[Singular startSession:...]` → `startNewSessionOrContinueSavedSession` → `copyFromPasteboard:`, which reads the clipboard on the main thread.
**Why now:** Our code: release 0.7.11 (71) was created 2026-11-09; whether Singular was added or changed in it is not checked. Dependencies: Singular SDK. Client/environment: one iPhone on iOS 27.2.1. Really new: first event with this stack.
**Hypothesis (not verified):** reading the pasteboard at launch can block while iOS fetches clipboard contents or shows its paste prompt.
**Related:** WHISPRNOTES-APP-4D (ignored) is also an App Hanging issue, but its stack is `AppDelegate.$main`, so per the recorded pattern it is not merged.
**Impact:** 1 event, 1 user.
**Classification:** needs attention, low. Possible fix (proposal): turn off Singular's clipboard attribution if it is not used.""",
}
for issue, text in notes.items():
    req = urllib.request.Request(f"https://sentry.obico.io/api/0/issues/{issue}/comments/", data=json.dumps({"text": text}).encode(),
                                 headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + TOKEN, "Content-Type": "application/json"}, method="POST")
    print(issue, json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60)).get("id"))
EOF
python3 $S/post_notes.py

content.text:
Six new Sentry alerts came in today, between 11:33 and 12:36 Pacific. Three were one-off tests from this machine, which I deleted. One was a repeat of an older JusPrin 1 bug, which I merged into the old issue. Two are real crashes, which I noted and left open. The translation of the Windows OpenGL dialog is running in its own session: [Translate upstream's Windows OpenGL dialog](#local_397ccdb1-7d53-4a98-b41f-b39b2f38bf4a).

**Deleted** under your one-off rule, with their emails trashed:
- **OBICO-SERVER-B2Q and B2R** (`KeyError: 'images'` and `KeyError: 'messages'`): two requests to the JusPrin 1 endpoints with incomplete bodies. They came from this machine's public IP (71.198.7.88) with the user agent "qa-check", right after release 4136, so another agent was most likely checking the release.
- **OBICO-SERVER-B2T** (`No module named 'web_ent'`): someone ran a `manage.py shell` command inside a production web pod with a wrong import. No user request failed. OBICO-SERVER-B1X was the same kind of mistake on 2026-11-07.

**Merged:** OBICO-SERVER-B2S went into OBICO-SERVER-AYH. I checked the Merged Issues tab, and it shows only the two matching fingerprints.
- **What failed:** a JusPrin 1 user on Windows sent a chat message, and the server's slicing step failed. The AI service asked the model to pick a process preset name from a list, and it rejected the name the model returned.
- **Likely cause (my hypothesis):** the preset name contains a 3MF file name with garbled Cyrillic and invisible control characters. The model's copy of the name probably drops those characters, so it never matches the list exactly. AYH had the same failure in September with a garbled Chinese file name.
- **Size:** 10 events and 2 users since July. It only affects JusPrin 1.

**Noted and left open:**
- **OBICO-MOBILE-24S:** the Android app 2.42 crashes on the printer list. `PrinterItem.js:48` reads `primaryWebcam.name` when a printer has no webcam marked as primary. The fix would be one character, `primaryWebcam?.name`. Version 2.42 is the first build with working source maps. OBICO-MOBILE-21A has the same message (22 events, 12 users since April, iOS and Android), but its stack has no app source lines, so I cross-referenced the two instead of merging them. My guess is they're the same bug.
- **WHISPRNOTES-APP-5P:** Whispr Notes on iOS hung for 2 seconds at launch inside the Singular attribution SDK, which reads the clipboard on the main thread. It's one event from one user. The older App Hanging issue has a different stack, so I didn't merge them.

I recorded the merge and the unmerged mobile pair in the triage skill's patterns file, and logged the run.

Should I make the one-line fix for the mobile printer-list crash in TSDApp now, or leave it for later?

content.text:
You're right, it isn't a new issue. It's an old crash that Sentry filed under a new fingerprint, because 2.42 is the first build that uploads its source maps.

**The crashing line is old.** `PrinterItem.js:48` reads `primaryWebcam.name`. It was added on 2024-07-10, and the code that picks `primaryWebcam` dates from 2024-05-26. When a printer has several webcams and none is marked primary, or has no webcams list at all, `primaryWebcam` is undefined and the printer list crashes.

**2.42 changed nothing in the app's behavior.** The only commits since July are "Upload JS source maps to Sentry from Android and iOS release builds" and the version bump, both on 2026-11-11.

**Why it showed up now:** Sentry groups a crash by its stack. Before 2.42 the stacks were minified bundle offsets, and those crashes went to OBICO-MOBILE-21A: 22 events and 12 users since April, on iOS 2.33 and 2.40 and Android 2.40 and 2.41. With source maps, the same crash now has real file names and lines, so Sentry opened OBICO-MOBILE-24S for it. The skill's patterns file records the same thing happening with another source-mapped 2.42 crash, which was merged into its old minified issue.

I left them separate earlier because "Cannot read property 'name' of undefined" is a generic message, and 21A's stacks show no app line. Given the history above, I now think they're the same bug.

Should I merge OBICO-MOBILE-24S into OBICO-MOBILE-21A, or leave them separate? The one-line fix in TSDApp is still open whenever you want it.
